notes_b: «وَ قَالَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» opens the report with the Imam's words and no transmitter; the chain that follows («رَوَى ذَلِكَ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ ... عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ») ends at Abu Ja'far, so it is unclear whether Ali is the last link (rule 6); he is written as a single link only on the bare opening
«وَ رَوَاهُ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ» names a different transmitter for the same saying: a variant

notes_a: Al-Faqih's statement of his routes (طرق) to Masadah's book, with no saying: needs_ruling (rule 11). Three routes are written as three groups.

The text writes هارون and مسعدة once after «جميعا», but the first route does not pass through them, so no single shared tail fits all three; the two meeting routes are written in full.
«- رضي اللّه عنهما -» is a blessing and is left out.

notes_b: the Prophet speaks a one-sentence report with no transmitter (rule 11)

A judgement («قضى ... في») with no transmitter (rule 11): needs a ruling

notes_a: The speaker of the saying («قال الشيخ ... اطلبوه إلي») is known only by the title «الشيخ»; the identifying words sit in a dash-gloss («-يعني أبا القاسم رضي الله عنه-»), which is left out. A source known only by a title is a ruling case, so the last written link is روح.
«وكان شيخا مستورا» is a description, not a name.
notes_b: The speaker of the saying ("اطلبوه إلي لأنظره" and the verdict after it) is «الشيخ», a title alone (rule 1); the identity appears only in an editor's gloss between dashes, which is left out. Rule 6 says to set needs_ruling when the speaker cannot be settled
«وكان شيخا مستورا» is a description, left out

notes_a: Group 1: «أبي» and «محمد بن عبد الله» are co-transmitters of «حدثني» (جميعا); «أخيه علي» is one link (علي).

notes_b: Layth narrates in the first person («استقبلته») and the one he met, who speaks («فقال إني لم أصل الظهر بعد»), is not named in the text: rule 11 sets needs_ruling, and that speaker is not added
Saying 2 is the answer to Layth's question («أخبرني فلان عن فلان عن عائشة»); the answerer is again unnamed, so the group goes from Layth to the two «فلان» placeholders (unnamed) and then Aisha
«أبي» occurrence 1 is the compiler's father; «علي» occurrence 1 is the brother in «عن أخيه علي» (rule 7)

notes_a: Level 1 has «حدثني أبي» and «محمد بن عبد الله بن جعفر الحميري» as co-transmitters («جميعا»).

notes_b: Umm Sa'id narrates her own encounter («قالت دخلت المدينة»); the speaker of the saying is Husayn b. Fatima, the last link after the narrator (owner ruling 5)

Ali's words are the saying; «أبيه» before «أمير المؤمنين» is one link (rule 7); the Sadiq's answer and the Prophet's citation are quoted inside saying 1 and have no own chain
«عليهما السلام» and «رضي الله عنه» are not part of any surface
notes_b: Two sayings, each with its own isnad (rule 4a): the Hasan answer, and a later anecdote where علي بن الحسين cites أبي, أخيه الحسن, أبيه أمير المؤمنين.

notes_a: The text opens «قال سفيان» with no written head, so Sufyan is the first named link.

«عليه السلام» is not part of the surface

notes_b: The father's answer («فقال: قال: كلهم من قريش») is in the scene, not a route; the Prophet is the end and is not written as a link

notes_a: No transmitter: the report opens with a narration of Ali's judgment (وَ أُتِيَ عَلِيٌّ ... فَلَمْ يُضَمِّنْهُ) and his words (إِنَّمَا هُوَ أَمِينٌ). This is the «قضى أمير المؤمنين ... في» case with no transmitter (rule 11), so groups is empty and the ruling is flagged.

notes_b: No transmitter: the report is Ali's judgement on a bathhouse attendant («وَ أُتِيَ عَلِيٌّ ... فَلَمْ يُضَمِّنْهُ وَ قَالَ»), read as a single-link route (rule 10)
A judgement by an Imam with no transmitter (rule 11): needs a ruling

notes_a: This is a rescript (توقيع) from an Imam that is not named in the text: rule 11 sends it to a ruling. «خرج على يد الشيخ أبي القاسم الحسين بن روح» names the conveyor of the rescript, not a transmitter; he is not added (rule 9). «أخبرنا جماعة» is unnamed (rule 8). «خرج على يد الشيخ أبي القاسم الحسين بن روح» and «خرج التوقيع» are the transmission of the rescript, not a link
